builders.angle: LITERAL -- the angle that won rounds 20 and 23. Work BRIEF-r24's fix list 1 to 4 in order and exactly as written, one wing at a time in the order the brief lists them, finishing each wing -- its drawn subject, its built walls, its darks, every room of it -- before starting the next. Read how rounds 22 and 23 built their wings first and do the same.

THE OBJECT FIRST -- the angle that won round 22 and won three screens of round 23. Start from each wing's subject -- the crib, the four-poster, the bookcase full of books, the skull niche -- and make each a drawn object with a silhouette a child could name, turned and carved detail, its own shading and a contact shadow, at the scale of the Kid; then build each room around it.

FOUR DIFFERENT HOUSES. The survey's sharpest line was that the Sleeping Quarters 'copy the Nursery's portraits-and-cabinets template'. Give each wing its own architecture first -- a child's room of painted panelling and a frieze, a bedchamber of damask and carved wainscot, a library of galleried oak, a crypt of stone vaults -- so no two read as one template re-lit, then furnish each with its drawn subject. Item 1 is still the test.
